narrative: The model estimates a 32% probability that you will fail your final year. That is not a certainty, but it is high enough that the model classifies you as needing remedial courses. The strongest signal was your plan for further study: you do not want to pursue higher education, whereas every passing student in the comparison group did. This was the top factor pushing the prediction toward failing. The second strongest factor was your reason for choosing this school: selecting it mainly for home-related reasons worked in your favor and pulled the prediction toward passing. The third strongest factor was your past record: you have one previous class failure, while students who passed had none on average, so this pushed toward failing. Two other practical warning signs are your eight absences, more than double the passing average of about four, and your weekly study time of under two hours, while most passing students studied two to five hours. To improve your chances, meet your counselor to plan the remedial work, set a clear academic goal, attend every class, and build a regular study schedule. Ask about school or paid subject support and use your family’s support. These steps address the strongest warning signs and make passing more likely.
